feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for senior digital/public-sector roles: the experience shows clear progression, relevant scope, and solid platform/communications leadership. It is well written overall, but impact would improve with tighter structure, less repetition across skills sections, and more outcome-focused metrics beyond activity descriptions.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear senior positioning: the headline, summary, and career progression strongly support a digital platform/communications leadership profile.  
- Good credibility and scale signals: 10,000+ page migration, 3.5M annual page views, 50+ publishers, and named tools/platforms add substance.  
- Writing is polished and professional, with no obvious misspellings; tone is consistent and appropriate for mission-driven/public-sector work.

1. Top improvements  
- Reduce duplication: “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT” overlap heavily. Consolidating these would improve scannability and save space.  
- Add more measurable outcomes: several bullets describe responsibilities (“led,” “developed,” “advised”) but fewer show results such as engagement growth, efficiency gains, adoption, or campaign performance.  
- Fix minor style/grammar inconsistencies: “social, and multimedia” has an unnecessary comma; date style varies (“Oct.”, “Sept.”, “Mar.”); “A2/Learning” is awkward—use “A2 (learning)” instead. Also consider whether “Coleman DAVIS” all-caps surname is intentional, as it may look inconsistent.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible intro with clear seniority and domain focus. It reads well, but it’s slightly dense and overlaps with the subtitle, core competencies, and work experience.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Tighten to one sharper value proposition and foreground public-sector scale/results.
- Replace generic phrasing like “building the platforms” with more direct action verbs such as “leading” or “modernizing.”
- Consider a rewrite: “Digital platform and communications leader with 12+ years of experience modernizing high-volume public-sector websites, governance models, analytics, and content operations. Leads enterprise web transformation, editorial systems, multimedia production, and AI-enabled user experiences for complex, mission-driven organizations.”
- Standardize style: use either “12+ years” or “more than 12 years” consistently across the CV; “AI-enabled” is correctly hyphenated.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Digital leader” overlaps with the subtitle “Digital Platform & Communications Systems Leader.”
- The list of capabilities closely repeats Core Competencies; keep the intro higher-level and less list-like.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block overlaps heavily with the header, Topline Skills, and Technical + IT sections. It would be stronger if tightened to emphasize leadership-level capabilities rather than repeating detailed skill categories.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Reframe as broader, executive-level competencies: Enterprise web modernization • Digital governance and content operations • Analytics, reporting, and performance insights • Cross-channel communications leadership • AI-enabled search and discovery • Workflow automation and platform integration • Public-sector advocacy communications • Multimedia and livestream production
- Standardize style: use “and” instead of mixing “&” with “and” for a cleaner, more formal tone.
- Consider replacing “editorial systems” with “content operations” to better match the language used across recent roles.
- If space allows, prioritize the most senior/recent strengths first: web modernization, governance, analytics, AI-enabled search.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section substantially duplicates the header summary and Topline Skills; keep it high-level and avoid tool-specific phrasing.
- “Multimedia production and livestream operations” overlaps with the dedicated Multimedia/Technical sections.
feedback.footer:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant project snapshot, but it largely repeats accomplishments already covered in Work Experience. Tightening phrasing and adding clearer outcomes or scope would make it feel more distinct and higher impact.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Rename to “Selected Recent Projects” and use concise, parallel phrasing: project name + action + result/focus.
- Add 1 concrete qualifier where possible (audience, platform, scale, campaign purpose, conference/event context) to increase specificity.
- Standardize style and punctuation; “10×20-foot” is fine, but keep all entries in the same verb tense and structure.
- Consider this tighter version:  
  • AI Hybrid Search — Designed an AI-enabled legislative search experience using hybrid retrieval, vector search, structured content workflows, and bill-level chat to improve policy-content discovery.  
  • We Are Counties Microsite — Built a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling modules, and downloadable resources in a modular architecture for ongoing expansion.  
  • Organization Anniversary Campaign — Developed a multi-part digital campaign featuring editorial storytelling, archival media, web features, and an interactive 10×20-foot conference display.  
  • Advocacy Video Series — Launched a recurring advocacy video series spanning editorial planning, production, and distribution across web, email, and social.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- AI Hybrid Search, microsite work, and advocacy video series closely overlap with Work Experience bullets; this section should emphasize standout examples, not restate responsibilities.

Leads enterprise web modernization, analytics infrastructure, editorial systems, multimedia production and AI-enabled user experiences for complex, mission-driven organizations.

items.title: Email

items.title: Website

items.title: Core Competencies
items.content: Enterprise website modernization • Digital governance & editorial systems • Analytics and reporting infrastructure • Multi-channel communications operations • AI-enabled search and content experiences • Workflow automation and platform integration • Advocacy and public-sector communications • Multimedia production and livestream operations

items.title: CV Footer
items.content:
### Recent Projects
**AI Hybrid Search**
Designed an AI-enabled legislative search experience combining hybrid retrieval, structured content workflows, vector search and bill-level AI chat to improve discovery of complex policy content.
**We Are Counties Microsite**
Built a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling modules, downloadable resources and a modular structure designed for continued campaign growth.
**Organization Anniversary Campaign**
Developed a multi-part digital campaign combining editorial storytelling, archival media, web features and a 10×20-foot interactive conference display connected to the main site.
**Advocacy Video Series**
Built a recurring advocacy video program spanning editorial planning, production and distribution across website, email and social channels.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Consult a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with good scope, but it reads as a service list rather than a results-oriented consulting entry. It also overlaps heavily with the Recent Projects section and prior NACo roles, so the bullets should emphasize what is new in this engagement.

Suggested edit
- Open with a sharper positioning line: “Advise NACo on enterprise digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations, and AI-enabled web modernization.”
- Consolidate overlapping bullets into 3–4 impact-focused bullets; e.g. combine systems/workflows/analytics/governance into one operations bullet.
- Add measurable outcomes where possible: number of sites/campaigns launched, publishers supported, toolkit downloads, search accuracy gains, reduced publishing time, or engagement improvements.
- Use stronger consulting verbs: “Advised,” “Designed,” “Implemented,” “Led,” “Optimized.” Example: “Led an AI-enabled search initiative, defining retrieval architecture, structured content workflows, and discovery UX for complex policy content.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Microsite structures, modular content sections, downloadable toolkits” duplicates the Recent Projects section; keep this item higher-level.
- “Governance, workflows, analytics” closely repeats the 2022–2024 Director role unless framed as post-tenure consulting/modernization work.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale metrics. It will be stronger if you tighten the opening, foreground the biggest outcomes, and avoid repeating channel-management details covered in the prior NACo role.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the broad lead sentence with a sharper scope/outcome summary: “Directed NACo’s digital media function across web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget management.”
- Lead with the website modernization win and keep the metrics: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page Drupal website serving 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Make channel oversight more outcome-oriented; add performance if available (growth, open rates, engagement, production volume) rather than “reaching tens of thousands.”
- Tighten remaining bullets with action + result phrasing: “Built NACo’s first in-house broadcast studio…,” “Implemented GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery reporting…,” “Established governance and publishing standards to improve cross-department coordination.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director entry.
- Video-programming language also echoes the older advocacy video bullets; emphasize studio buildout and operational scale here.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps heavily with the adjacent NACo roles and reads more like a bridge role than a distinct step up. Make it tighter and emphasize what was owned or expanded at this level before the broader leadership scope in the next role.

Suggested edit:
- Open with scope + progression: “Managed day-to-day digital communications operations across NACo’s web, email, social and video channels, strengthening editorial coordination and advocacy messaging.”
- Tighten bullets to distinct contributions: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Rephrase video bullet to show growth/ownership: “Produced and scaled a weekly advocacy video update into a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Combine planning/workflow bullets: “Improved cross-team editorial planning and digital publishing workflows across communications, advocacy and program teams.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video” is very close to the Director of Digital Media entry; avoid repeating channel lists.
- Weekly video/update language also overlaps with the earlier Digital Media Manager / Producer role and footer project list.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this skills block is too generic and overlaps heavily with the header and Core Competencies. Tighten it to emphasize senior leadership scope and public-sector relevance without repeating wording used elsewhere.

Suggested edit:
- Replace broad phrases with sharper, executive-level language:
- Enterprise digital strategy for high-volume public-sector organizations
- Editorial governance, publishing standards, and content operations
- Cross-channel communications leadership across web, email, social, and video
- Advocacy and public-sector messaging strategy
- Audience-centered content planning and information design
- Consider swapping “Multi-channel communications leadership” for “Cross-channel communications operations” only if you want closer alignment with recent NACo roles.
- If space allows, make one item outcome-oriented, e.g., “Enterprise digital strategy for 10,000+ page, 3.5M annual-view web ecosystems.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy” and “Editorial systems and governance” duplicate both the header summary and Core Competencies almost verbatim.
- “Audience-focused content planning” is weaker and less distinctive than experience-based strengths like governance, analytics, or platform modernization.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster, but it reads as a generic tool list and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” section. This topline version should be tighter, more strategic, and emphasize the platforms most tied to recent impact.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from a long inventory to a curated strengths line: “Drupal and CMS modernization • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript) • API integrations and workflow automation • Airtable-based operational systems • AI-enabled search experiences”
- Prioritize recent, proven strengths: lead with Drupal, CMS modernization, AI-enabled search, and integrations; demote or remove older/less evidenced platforms like WordPress and SharePoint if space is tight.
- Cut “jQuery” unless specifically required for target roles; it dates the profile and adds little at topline level.
- If you want one stronger phrasing option: “Drupal platform delivery • CMS modernization • Front-end web implementation • API and workflow integrations • Airtable systems • AI-enabled search”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item duplicates the detailed “Technical + IT” section; keep topline strategic, not exhaustive.
- “AI-enabled search experiences” also appears in Core Competencies, so avoid repeating identical wording elsewhere.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster for recent leadership roles, but it reads as a raw tool list and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” analytics section. Make it more outcome-oriented and executive-level.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools-only to capability + decision impact: “Analytics strategy, reporting and optimization” rather than just platforms.
- Tighten and group related items: “GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI, Microsoft Clarity” instead of separate bullets if space is tight.
- Replace generic phrases with stronger wording: use “Executive KPI frameworks” instead of “KPI design,” and “Leadership dashboards and decision support” instead of “Leadership reporting.”
- Suggested rewrite: “GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI and Microsoft Clarity • Executive KPI frameworks and dashboarding • SEO, UX and performance analysis • Insight generation for digital optimization”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This substantially duplicates “Technical + IT > Data, Analytics & Optimization”; keep Topline Skills higher-level and save full tool inventory for Technical + IT.
- “SEO and performance analysis” may overlap with broader digital strategy language elsewhere; keep only if SEO is a target requirement.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong skill area, but this item is generic and overlaps heavily with the Core Competencies line and multiple NACo roles. Make it more distinctive by emphasizing production scope, technical depth, and delivery context rather than broad labels.

Suggested edit
- Replace with tighter, more specific phrasing:
- Broadcast-quality video production and post-production
- Livestream and hybrid event production
- PTZ camera and studio system operation
- Virtual event technical direction and run-of-show delivery
- If space allows, add one higher-value qualifier such as “in-house studio production” or “advocacy and member-facing programming.”
- Keep terms parallel and noun-based; avoid mixing broad categories (“studio operations”) with vague formats (“livestreaming”).
- Consider “technical direction” over “event delivery” if you want a more senior, operational tone.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Multimedia production and livestream operations” already appears in Core Competencies; avoid repeating the same wording.
- “Studio operations” and “hybrid/virtual event production” are already supported by the Director of Digital Media entry, so this skills line should stay concise and specialized.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it’s too bare and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution.” Since Drupal is central to recent roles, this item should either sharpen that emphasis or be consolidated.

Suggested edit:
- Reorder by relevance/recency: **Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- Add light qualifiers only where they reinforce recent impact, e.g. **Drupal (enterprise migration, microsites, modular content)** if your format allows.
- If keeping as a standalone skills line, consider tightening to: **Drupal (enterprise/public-sector) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- Alternatively, rename the category to **CMS & Web Publishing Platforms** to better distinguish it from coding/integration tools.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This is largely duplicated by **Topline Skills → Web Platforms & Technical Execution**; consider removing one version or making this one more platform-specific and the other more execution-focused.
- Drupal impact is already demonstrated strongly in recent experience, so avoid overloading multiple sections with the same generic list.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical breadth, but this reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. Tighten it to emphasize implementation tools you actively use in recent roles and group items more strategically.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: **Front-end & implementation:** HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, jQuery • **Integrations & tagging:** API integrations, Google Tag Manager • **Deployment & edge tooling:** Cloudflare Workers, GitHub Actions
- Consider dropping version numbers (“HTML5,” “CSS3”) unless required; “HTML, CSS, JavaScript” is cleaner and more current.
- If accurate, add scope or outcome in adjacent experience bullets instead of here, e.g., “built custom Drupal front-end components,” “deployed workflow automations via GitHub Actions,” or “implemented GTM for analytics/event tracking.”
- Order by relevance to recent work: JavaScript/API integrations/GTM/Cloudflare Workers/GitHub Actions first; jQuery last.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Duplicates “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” and “API integrations” already listed under Topline Skills.
- GTM may also fit under analytics; keep it here only if positioned as implementation rather than reporting.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this item is too broad and reads like a generic software list. It also overlaps with “Workflow automation and platform integration” in Core Competencies and “Airtable systems / Workflow automation” in Topline Skills, so it should emphasize systems actually tied to recent leadership work.

Suggested edit:
- Split by function to improve scanability and reduce “tool dump” feel: “Automation: Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier | Project/work management: Jira, Asana, Trello, Basecamp | Collaboration: Slack, Teams”
- Consider renaming to “Workflow Automation & Collaboration Tools” so the heading matches the contents.
- Prioritize tools most relevant to recent roles; if space is tight, cut older/lower-signal items like Basecamp or Trello.
- If accurate, add a light qualifier in another section rather than here, e.g., “built cross-team workflows in Airtable and Power Automate,” since impact is better shown in experience bullets than in skills lists.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Airtable” and “workflow automation” already appear in Topline Skills/Core Competencies.
- Slack and Teams are common workplace tools; they add little unless collaboration platforms are central to the role.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant tools, but this item is too bare compared with the rest of the CV and misses a chance to signal enterprise-scale email/engagement capability. It should emphasize platform depth and align with the recent NACo work leading email operations.

Suggested edit
- Rename to: **Email Marketing & Member Engagement Platforms**
- Reorder by likely relevance/scale: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp**
- If accurate, add scope wording in the item title or nearby skills summary, e.g. **enterprise email automation, newsletter operations, audience segmentation**
- Consider a tighter phrasing style consistent with other technical items: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights/Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp**

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- This overlaps with work-experience bullets about leading email newsletters and digital channels; keep this item tool-focused only, not responsibility-focused.
- “Multi-channel communications operations” already appears in Core Competencies, so avoid adding generic engagement language without platform-specific detail.

items.title: Data, Analytics & Optimization
items.content: GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • Looker Studio • Power BI • BigQuery • SEO • A/B testing • Dashboarding
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tools list, but it overlaps heavily with “Topline Skills > Analytics, Insights & Optimization” and misses a chance to show depth or business use. In this section, make it more technical and concise rather than repeating broad concepts.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: **GA4 • BigQuery • Power BI • Looker Studio • Microsoft Clarity • Google Tag Manager • SEO analysis • Experimentation**
- Replace **A/B testing** with **Experimentation** if formal testing platforms/processes were used; it sounds more senior and broader.
- Replace **Dashboarding** with either a specific tool/process or remove it; dashboarding is already implied by Power BI/Looker Studio.
- If accurate, add one higher-signal technical item such as **KPI framework design**, **data visualization**, or **event tracking** to show applied analytics capability.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item substantially duplicates Topline Skills [3]; consider trimming one of the two or making this version more tool-specific.
- GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery are already named in the 2022–2024 role, so avoid repeating generic terms here.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal, but the item is still broad and overlaps with later NACo roles. Make it more foundational and execution-focused, with any concrete scale you can add.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to emphasize early-team building and hands-on delivery: “Promoted through two digital roles to help establish NACo’s first in-house digital team and formalize workflows across web, email, social and multimedia.”
- Add clearer outcomes where possible: website refresh scope, livestream/event volume, video cadence, audience growth, or efficiency gains.
- Tighten the close to show leadership without overstating seniority: “Produced livestreams and weekly video updates and provided day-to-day direction to a digital media associate.”
- Optional full rewrite: “Promoted through two digital roles to help build NACo’s first in-house digital team, improve cross-channel publishing workflows, support a major website refresh, and produce recurring livestream and video content while guiding a junior team member.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 advocacy video bullet; differentiate this as the earlier launch/build phase.
- “strengthening workflows” repeats language used in later NACo entries; make this role more tactical/foundational.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry, but it reads generic and overlaps with later NACo roles in digital/media. Emphasize the podcast launch as the clearest differentiator and tighten the research/program support language.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to foreground the unique achievement: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting NACo programs and policy priorities.”
- Make the second sentence more specific and concise: “Produced digital and multimedia content for member communications, including launching NACo’s first podcast and leading episode planning, scripting and production.”
- If accurate, add scope or outcome: number of episodes, audience, internal stakeholders supported, or how the podcast/content advanced advocacy or member engagement.
- Remove filler like “contributed to” and “materials”; use stronger verbs such as coordinated, produced, launched, led.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Podcast/multimedia work overlaps with later digital roles; keep this entry focused on “first podcast” and innovation/research support, not general digital operations.
- Avoid broad claims about web/email/social here, since those are covered more strongly in 2015–2024 roles.

items.title: Multimedia & Creative Tools
